headline: BSF-BGB meeting in Delhi: Both sides pledge to maintain peace along border
summary: The 57th DG-level border coordination conference concluded in New Delhi without a joint press conference, focusing on border killings and smuggling.
details: The 57th Director General (DG) level border coordination conference between the Border Security Force (BSF) and Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) concluded on Thursday in New Delhi.
The four-day event, held at the BSF headquarters, ended with the signing of joint discussion documents, though no joint press conference was held, departing from usual customs.
The BGB Director General expressed deep concern over border killings and violence, emphasizing the need to reduce such incidents along the shared boundary.
Key agenda items included addressing 'push-ins' and illegal infiltration, as well as combating the smuggling of drugs, weapons, and other prohibited items.

caption:
BGB and BSF conclude 57th border conference in Delhi. Border killings and smuggling remain top priorities.

The 57th Director General (DG) level border coordination conference between the Border Security Force (BSF) and Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) concluded on Thursday in New Delhi.

The four-day event, held at the BSF headquarters, ended with the signing of joint discussion documents, though no joint press conference was held, departing from usual customs.

The BGB Director General expressed deep concern over border killings and violence, emphasizing the need to reduce such incidents along the shared boundary.

Key agenda items included addressing 'push-ins' and illegal infiltration, as well as combating the smuggling of drugs, weapons, and other prohibited items.

Both forces agreed to strengthen joint patrols and enhance the exchange of information to ensure stability and security along the border.

Historically, DG-level meetings were held annually from 1975 to 1992, but since 1993, they have been scheduled twice a year, alternating between New Delhi and Dhaka.

headline: SpaceX valuation tops $2 trillion after record-breaking Nasdaq debut
summary: The company raised $75 billion in its IPO, more than double the proceeds of Saudi Aramco's record listing.
details: SpaceX shares jumped 23 percent in its Nasdaq debut on Friday, pushing the company's market value above $2 trillion. This makes it the sixth-largest US company by market capitalization.
The landmark IPO raised $75 billion, more than double the proceeds of Saudi Aramco's record-setting 2019 listing. The stock opened at $150 and was last trading at $166 per share.
The listing cements Elon Musk's status as the first trillionaire ever, despite the firm posting a loss of nearly $5 billion last year.
Market analysts are closely watching the debut as a signal for future mega-listings, including AI heavyweights like OpenAI and Anthropic.
SpaceX is expected to be fast-tracked into the Nasdaq 100 index, which will likely increase demand from passive funds and ETFs.
While some analysts praise Musk's vision, others warn that the valuation is lofty, with a price-to-revenue ratio of 94 based on 2025 revenue projections of $18.7 billion.
The debut caused a reshuffling in the investor portfolio, leading to sharp declines in shares of other space and satellite firms like Planet Labs and EchoStar.
caption:
SpaceX just hit a $2 trillion valuation. Elon Musk becomes the world's first trillionaire.

SpaceX shares jumped 23 percent in its Nasdaq debut on Friday, pushing the company's market value above $2 trillion. This makes it the sixth-largest US company by market capitalization.

The landmark IPO raised $75 billion, more than double the proceeds of Saudi Aramco's record-setting 2019 listing. The stock opened at $150 and was last trading at $166 per share.

The listing cements Elon Musk's status as the first trillionaire ever, despite the firm posting a loss of nearly $5 billion last year.

Market analysts are closely watching the debut as a signal for future mega-listings, including AI heavyweights like OpenAI and Anthropic.

SpaceX is expected to be fast-tracked into the Nasdaq 100 index, which will likely increase demand from passive funds and ETFs.

While some analysts praise Musk's vision, others warn that the valuation is lofty, with a price-to-revenue ratio of 94 based on 2025 revenue projections of $18.7 billion.

The debut caused a reshuffling in the investor portfolio, leading to sharp declines in shares of other space and satellite firms like Planet Labs and EchoStar.
